# Papercut kit catalog (generated by tools/catalog.py; do not edit)

The kit is synced into each project at `src/lib/` (`papercut/sync_kit.sh`). Scenes import it as `../lib/<file>`.
Read this file instead of the kit source. Open a source file only when you need a detail that isn't here.
If a scene needs something the kit lacks, build it in your scene file. The lead promotes reusable pieces into the kit after the episode (HARVEST.md).

## `fonts.ts`  (import from `'../lib/fonts'`)

> Fonts from local files in public/fonts/: the exact woff2 files @remotion/google-fonts used to fetch at render time. Two problems this fixes: 1. Network: every render tab fetched the fonts from fonts.gstatic.com, so a Wi-Fi blip failed the whole render. 2. Banner jitter: TapeBanner sizes its text with fitText(). ## `paper/backdrops.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/backdrops'`)

> Backdrops: 24 paper-diorama sets (1080x1920 JPEGs in public/bg/backdrops/) to use instead of <Room>, so each scene can sit in its own place. Layout contract for every set: floor line near y 1420 (measured per set in BACKDROPS), calm middle band for props and UI, calm top for the banner, plain bottom for captions, light from the top-left, no people or text baked in. Stand props and critters on BACK

- `const BACKDROPS = {`: Every backdrop name with its measured floor line (px y at 1080x1920) and mood (day, night, warm, cool). Props and critters stand on floorY.
- `type BackdropName = keyof typeof BACKDROPS;`: Union of the backdrop names, for typing a scene's `backdrop` prop.
- `<Backdrop name: BackdropName; tint?: string; dim?: number>`: Backdrop: full-frame generated set (object-fit cover), a drop-in for <Room>. Optional `tint` multiplies a colour over it, `dim` (0-1) darkens it toward black.

## `paper/camera.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/camera'`)

> Camera moves for papercut sets: parallax orbit (OrbitCamera + Depth layers), foreground pass, rack focus, snap zoom, pull-back reveal and freeze frame. A fake camera moving through a paper diorama; all motion from useCurrentFrame(). Moves transform the whole frame, so the banner zone (y < 420) and the caption band (y 1420-1580) move too: keep key props and faces out of both.

- `<OrbitCamera dur: number; yaw?: number; drift?: [number, number]; push?: number; focus?: number; depth?: number; origin?: [number, number]; children: React.ReactNode>`: Parallax orbit: the camera arcs `yaw` degrees (16) around the focal plane while dollying to `push`, so <Depth z> layers separate. `origin` = pivot px (near the floor line), `depth` = layer spacing, `drift` = pan px.
- `<Depth z: number; cover?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Depth layer in <OrbitCamera>: z 0 = backdrop (auto-oversized to cover), ~0.5 = props and cast, 1 = foreground. Lay each out at normal screen positions; the camera adds the parallax. Outside an OrbitCamera it is a plain fill.
- `<ForegroundPass at: number; dur?: number; kind?: 'leaf' | 'cable' | 'block'; from?: 'left' | 'right'; y?: number; blur?: number; scale?: number; dim?: number>`: Blurred paper object (kind leaf | cable | block) sweeps across the lens from the `from` side over `dur` frames from `at`, and a faint shadow dims the set. Put it last in the stack; `y` moves its anchor.
- `<RackFocus from?: number; to?: number; at?: number; dur?: number; bleed?: boolean; returnAt?: number; holdFrames?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Blur wrapper: eases blur `from` to `to` px over `dur` frames from `at`. Wrap the backdrop (set `bleed` to hide its soft edge) or a hero prop; use opposite pairs on two planes to pull focus between them. `returnAt` / `holdFrames` make it a …
- `<SnapZoom at: number; x?: number; y?: number; to?: number; settle?: number; shake?: number; roll?: number; blur?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Punch-in to the focal point (x, y): 1 to `to` (1.25) in 4 frames with radial motion blur, a 3-frame shake and a little roll, then settles at `settle`. For numbers and joke landings: `at` = the frame the thing lands.
- `<PullBack dur: number; x: number; y: number; from?: number; at?: number; blur?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Pull-back reveal: starts `from`x (2.8) tight on the detail at (x, y), eases out to the whole set over `dur` frames with motion blur on the first frames. Edges stay covered. Shows scale.
- `<FreezeFrame at: number; label?: string; x?: number; y?: number; rot?: number; size?: number; mark?: 'left' | 'right' | false; children: React.ReactNode>`: Meme beat: holds the child on frame `at` (Freeze), desaturates, darkens the edges, then slaps on a torn paper `label` (at x, y) with a stamp bounce and a record-scratch mark (left|right). Pair with SFX `scratch` at `at`.
- `<DollyZoom dur: number; at?: number; strength?: number; grow?: number; focus?: number; depth?: number; origin?: [number, number]; children: React.ReactNode>`: Dolly zoom for the REALISATION beat ("oh no"): the subject layer (z = focus) holds its size, near layers swell and the backdrop shrinks and spreads. Build it from <Depth z> layers. `strength` 1.5; <1 reverses.
- `const crabFrames = (stops: number[], hold = 14, move = 10) => stops.length * hold + (stops.length - 1) * move;`: Total frames a CrabTrack takes: a hold at every stop and a move between stops.
- `<CrabTrack stops: number[]; hold?: number; move?: number; at?: number; parallax?: number; focus?: number; blur?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Crab track (a flat side-on track) for LISTS, lineups and comparisons: slides along a set wider than the frame, easing to each x in `stops` (world px) and holding `hold` frames. Put layers in <Depth> (z 0.45 = items).
- `<Crane dur: number; height: number; mode?: 'rise' | 'drop'; at?: number; pitch?: number; parallax?: number; focus?: number; blur?: boolean; origin?: [number, number]; children: React.ReactNode>`: Crane for SCALE reveals and "meanwhile, below": a vertical move through a tall set (layers in <Depth>, world y = screen y at the top). `drop` descends `height` px through dollhouse floors; `rise` climbs and tilts to a high angle.
- `<PovMask kind?: 'keyhole' | 'lens' | 'binoculars' | 'phone'; x?: number; y?: number; size?: number; reticle?: boolean; at?: number; sway?: number; zoom?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: POV mask for SPY and PRIVACY beats: the child is seen through a paper keyhole, lens, binoculars or phone viewfinder (`kind`) in a dark surround, with handheld sway and a crosshair `reticle`. (x, y) = view centre; `at` = raise frame.
- `<TimeRamp segments: {until: number; rate: number}[]; start?: number; trail?: boolean; push?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Time ramp (speed ramp / bullet time) for the DRAMATIC beat: remaps the child's clock. `segments` = [{until (outer frame), rate}]: 0.2 = slow-mo, 0 = frozen, >1 = fast with a trail; 1 after the last. `start` = inner frame at 0.
- `<DutchTilt deg?: number; at?: number; judder?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Dutch tilt for "things going wrong": the frame rolls to `deg` (10) with a back-ease snap from `at`, then judders on twos. Scaled up so the rotated frame still covers the canvas (a big crop at 1080 x 1920, so keep key props central).
- `<TiltShift focus?: number; band?: number; blur?: number; sat?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Tilt shift for MINIATURE scale ("a tiny paper world"): blurs the top and bottom bands so the diorama reads as a toy model, and lifts saturation. `focus` = sharp band centre (0-1), `band` = its height, `blur` = px at the edges.
- `<FocusPulse at: number; dur?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Focus pulse, the hunt alone on a static shot: it goes soft and snaps back over `dur` frames (18) from `at`. For REVEALS and emphasis (a number lands, a prop is named) without moving the camera.
- `<FocusHunt at: number; dur?: number; amount?: number; x?: number; y?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Focus hunt for REVEALS: pushes in on a number or key prop at (x, y) from 1x to 1+`amount` (1 = 2x) over `dur` frames (30) with a hard ease, and the lens hunts for focus part-way through (starts at 10/30 of dur, lasts 18/30).
- `<Handheld amount?: number; roll?: number; rate?: number; settleAt?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: ---------- handheld ---------- Handheld camera for lit-by-fire and tense scenes: a slow, deterministic multi-sine drift (x, y, roll) plus a faint breathing scale. `amount` = px of drift, `roll` = deg, `rate` = frames per drift cycle; `sett…

## `paper/look.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/look'`)

> Film-look layers for papercut reels: gate weave and exposure flicker (FilmWeave), moving felt fibre (FeltFibre), lens dirt, lamp flicker, print halftone and graph paper. Overlays use the textures in public/bg/textures/ (synced by sync_kit.sh). Keep every one of them subtle. Overlays sit above the set and below the banner and captions; FilmWeave wraps the set.

- `<FilmWeave amp?: number; flicker?: number; seed?: string; children: React.ReactNode>`: Film gate weave plus exposure flicker, for a photographed, stop-motion feel: the frame drifts about 1.5 px with a hair of rotation, stepped on twos, and brightness wobbles 2.5% (seeded). `amp` / `flicker` scale each (1 = default).
- `<FeltFibre opacity?: number; blend?: Blend>`: Moving felt-fibre overlay (felt-fibre.mp4, 12 fps on purpose, looped), a living alternative to GrainOverlay. The grey base is crushed to black so only the bright fibres show, then screened on at `opacity` 0.3.
- `<LensDirt opacity?: number; at?: number; x?: number; y?: number; r?: number; blend?: Blend>`: Lens dirt (smudges, dust) for lit dioramas and FocusHunt moments: screened on, so it lifts the darks; (x, y, r) confines it to a lamp or flash. `at` = fade-in frame. Subtle at best; color-dodge hits only highlights but washes cream paper.
- `const flickerAt = (f: number, seed = 'lamp', depth = 0.4, every = 42) => {`: The brightness multiplier (about 0.3-1.03) of a flickering light at frame f: a gentle shimmer plus an occasional organic dip and recovery. Seeded, so a render never changes. `depth` = how far a dip goes, `every` = frames per chance of one.
- `<LampFlicker seed?: string; depth?: number; every?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Wraps a light source's glow (a Glow, a lit lamp shade) so it flickers: occasional organic dips that recover, seeded per lamp. Use `flickerAt` for your own maths. Differ the `seed` between lamps.
- `<Halftone opacity?: number; tone?: number; at?: number; blend?: Blend; children?: React.ReactNode>`: Print texture for "newspaper", "report" and "leak document" beats: a scanned print grain multiplied over the frame. With children it also washes the colour toward newsprint (`tone` 0-1 desaturation). `opacity` 0.4.
- `<GraphPaper x?: number; y?: number; w?: number; h?: number; rot?: number; tint?: string; dim?: number; children?: React.ReactNode>`: Graph paper for plan, sketch and maths beats. With no box it is a full-frame backdrop (`tint` multiplies a colour, `dim` darkens); with (x, y, w, h) it is a paper card surface with the usual rough edge and shadow, tilted by `rot`.

## `paper/motion.ts`  (import from `'../lib/paper/motion'`)

> Small keyframe helpers every hand-animated scene reuses (so scene files do not each carry a copy). keyed = piecewise eased value through [frame, value] keys; swing = decaying follow-through; onN = stepped "on twos"; clamp01 and lcg are the usual 0-1 clamp and a seeded random.

- `const keyed = (f: number, keys: [number, number][], ease: (t: number) => number = Easing.out(Easing.cubic)) => {`
- `const swing = (f: number, at: number, amp: number, tau = 9, period = 14) =>`
- `const onN = (f: number, n = 2) => f - (f % n);`
- `const clamp01 = (v: number) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v));`
- `const lcg = (seed: number) => { let s = seed; return () => { s = (s * 1664525 + 1013904223) % 4294967296; return s / 4294967296; }; };`

## `paper/proof.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/proof'`)

> Proof beat: a real browser capture laid on a paper card (RealShot) with hand-drawn red marker strokes over it (MarkerCircle, MarkerUnderline, MarkerArrow). Use it once per reel, on the proof beat: it is the one place a real page, real logos and real UI appear. Capture the page with lib/tools/capture.mjs. Marker strokes are filled ribbons (varying width, rough ends) revealed by a stroke-dashoffset 

- `<RealShot src: string; x: number; y: number; w: number; ratio?: number; rot?: number; tape?: boolean; at?: number; chrome?: string; children?: React.ReactNode>`: A real screenshot (public/ PNG from tools/capture.mjs) on a paper card: tape corners, shadow, print grain, pop-in at `at`. `ratio` = image h/w (capture.mjs prints it); `chrome` = URL text for a paper browser bar; children share the tilt.
- `<MarkerCircle x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number; at: number; dur?: number; color?: string; loops?: number; seed?: string; width?: number; bleed?: boolean>`: Hand-drawn red marker ellipse around the centre (x, y), w x h, drawn on over `dur` frames from `at` (default 10). Overshoots its start (`loops` 1.15). `bleed` (on) = felt-tip ink: ragged edge, pooling at start and end. `width` = pen px.
- `<MarkerUnderline x: number; y: number; w: number; at: number; dur?: number; color?: string; double?: boolean; seed?: string; width?: number; bleed?: boolean>`: Hand-drawn red marker underline from (x, y) across `w` px, left to right, with a slight slope and wobble; `double` adds a second pass back underneath.
- `<MarkerArrow x: number; y: number; tx: number; ty: number; at: number; dur?: number; color?: string; bend?: number; seed?: string; width?: number; bleed?: boolean>`: Hand-drawn red marker arrow from (x, y) to the tip (tx, ty): a slightly bowed shaft, then two barbs. `bend` = how much the shaft bows (0.14 of its length).

## `paper/sets.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/sets'`)

> Set building blocks: a room per set (tinted paper wall + floor band), generated decor props, and the whip-pan into the CTA. Light from the top-left everywhere.

- `<Room color: RoomColor | string; floorY?: number; floor?: 'wood' | 'dark' | 'none'; skirting?: boolean>`: Room: flat wall colour × mottled paper wall texture (multiply) + vignette, then a floor band. floorY is the floor line (characters stand on it). Captions sit on the floor band (y ≈ 1430–1560); keep faces above y 1400.
- `<Plant x: number; y: number; s?: number>`: Decor props, cut from paper in code. (x, y) is the top-left; s scales the whole prop.
- `<Lamp x: number; y: number; s?: number; on?: boolean>`
- `<Corkboard x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number>`
- `<Window x: number; y: number; w?: number; h?: number; night?: boolean>`
- `<Shelf x: number; y: number; w: number; books?: number>`: Wall shelf with a few book spines.
- `<Sticky x: number; y: number; s?: number; color?: string; rot?: number>`: Sticky note on a wall.
- `<WhipIn dur?: number; from?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Whip-pan into a set: the frame arrives from the right with a horizontal motion smear (~7 frames).

## `paper/transitions.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/transitions'`)

> Paper transitions between scenes: whip, zoomThrough, pageTurn (curl), tearAway, tapePull (a kraft tape strip), stampCut, infiniteZoom (Droste), popUpBook (+ PopUpOpen) and keyhole. Use <CutSeries> in place of <Series> in PapercutVideo: cuts={{S05: {kind: 'pageTurn'}}}, keyed by the INCOMING scene, no entry = hard cut. Scene start frames stay on plan.json. Needs <PaperDefs/>.

- `type CutKind = 'whip' | 'zoomThrough' | 'pageTurn' | 'tearAway' | 'tapePull' | 'stampCut' | 'infiniteZoom' | 'popUpBook' | 'keyhole' | 'burnAway';`: Story beats: whip topic switch, zoomThrough go inside, pageTurn next step, tearAway something breaks, tapePull the default cut, stampCut verdict, infiniteZoom recursion joke, popUpBook chapter or opener, keyhole sneaking in / spying / a he…
- `const CUT_DEFAULTS: Record<CutKind, {frames: number; sfx: string}> = {`: Default frames and suggested SFX per kind: whip 7 'whip', zoomThrough 8 'zoom', pageTurn 12 'page-flip', tearAway 10 'rip', tapePull 10 'tape-peel', stampCut 12 'stamp' (+3 frames, on the thump), infiniteZoom 24 'zoom', popUpBook 20 'pop3'…
- `const whip = (o: {blur?: number; overlap?: number} = {}) => pres(Whip, o);`: whip, 7 frames, SFX whip: the outgoing scene shoots off left, the incoming arrives from the right, both with a strong horizontal motion smear. For a fast topic switch or a "meanwhile". blur = peak smear in px (46).
- `const zoomThrough = (o: {x?: number; y?: number; scale?: number; trails?: number} = {}) => pres(ZoomThrough, o);`: zoomThrough, 8 frames, SFX zoom: pushes hard into the focal point (x, y px) of the outgoing scene until it fills the frame and blurs; the incoming scene scales 1.15 -> 1 and unblurs. For going inside a screen, door or mirror.
- `const pageTurn = (o: {style?: 'curl' | 'fold'; angle?: number; from?: 'bottom' | 'top'; back?: string} = {}) => pres(PageTurn, o);`: pageTurn, 12 frames, SFX page-flip: the outgoing scene is a sheet of paper whose corner curls over like a book page (cylindrical highlight, paper back, cast shadow). For "next step", "turn the page", a new chapter. style 'fold' = flat fold…
- `const tearAway = (o: {x?: number; jag?: number; seed?: string} = {}) => pres(TearAway, o);`: tearAway, 10 frames, SFX rip: the outgoing scene rips in two along a jagged vertical tear (x px, default 540) with white fibrous edges; the halves fall away. For a broken promise, a leak, "ripped off", cancelling something. jag = roughness.
- `const tapePull = (o: {y?: number; label?: string} = {}) => pres(TapePull, o);`: tapePull, 10 frames, SFX tape-peel: a kraft strip (plain, or printed with `label`) slaps across the top of the outgoing sheet (y px, 175) and is yanked up, dragging the sheet off with a tilt and a flap. A good default cut.
- `const stampCut = (o: {x?: number; y?: number; ink?: string} = {}) => pres(StampCut, o);`: stampCut, 12 frames, SFX stamp: a 3/4-view paper rubber stamp slams into the middle (x, y px), squashes, shakes the sheet and springs out the top, leaving an inked impression with the incoming scene inside it, which grows to fill the frame…
- `const infiniteZoom = (o: {levels?: number; x?: number; y?: number; w?: number; bezel?: string} = {}) => pres(Droste, o);`: infiniteZoom, 24 frames, SFX zoom: Droste. A paper screen (x, y, w px) appears in the outgoing scene showing a smaller copy of it; the camera dives through `levels` nested copies (2) and lands in the incoming scene. For recursion jokes: ca…
- `const popUpBook = (o: {style?: 'dim' | 'kraft'} = {}) => pres(PopUpBook, o);`: popUpBook, 20 frames, SFX pop3: the previous scene dims, an open book slides up, and the incoming set rises out of its gutter as three pop-up cards (backdrop, props, foreground) with fold shadows. For a chapter change or "let me show you".…
- `const keyhole = (o: KeyholeOpts = {}) => pres(Keyhole, o);`: keyhole, 14 frames, SFX click: a heist iris. A near-black paper card closes over the outgoing scene leaving a keyhole window (middle at x, y px) that shrinks until shut, holds ~2 frames on black, then the window re-opens on the incoming sc…
- `const burnAway = (o: BurnOpts = {}) => pres(Burn, o);`: burnAway, 14 frames, SFX burn-away: the outgoing scene is paper that catches light. A glowing orange-red scorched edge eats outward from the ignition point (x, y px, default bottom-centre 540, 1500) along an irregular noise-driven front; t…
- `<PopUpOpen dur?: number; from?: number; table?: string; children: React.ReactNode>`: PopUpOpen: the popUpBook as an opener, with no outgoing scene. Wrap the first scene's set: the book is already open on frame 0 (from = starting progress, 0.15) and the set pops up over `dur` frames (20). table = what the book lies on (kraf…

## `props/cable.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/props/cable'`)

> Plugging in: a fat ribbed paper cable (a cubic curve between two points), a plug head that rides its end, and a socket plate to plug into. cablePath    builds the `d` for <Cable> from a start point S and an end point E, with a slack amount Cable        the ribbed cable along any SVG path `d` (full frame; coordinates are frame pixels) PlugHead     two-prong plug with a ribbed boot; place it on the 

- `type Pt = {x: number; y: number};`: A point in frame pixels (1080 x 1920).
- `const cablePath = (S: Pt, E: Pt, slack: number, sagS = 300, back = 150) => {`: Path for <Cable> from S to E: hangs from S, enters E from the left; slack 1 = lazy floor loop, 0 = near taut. Returns {d, c2}; aim a PlugHead along E - c2.
- `<Cable d: string; color?: string; lo?: string; hi?: string; width?: number>`: A fat ribbed paper cable drawn along the SVG path `d` (frame pixels, use cablePath or your own); `width` = thickness px, `color`/`lo`/`hi` = body, rib/shadow and highlight.
- `<PlugHead x: number; y: number; rot?: number; s?: number; boot?: string; bootLo?: string; bootHi?: string>`: Two-prong plug, about 140 px long at s = 1. (x, y) = middle of the connector body; it points right and `rot` (deg) turns it about that middle, `s` scales it. boot/bootLo/bootHi = the ribbed boot's colours.
- `<SocketPlate x: number; y: number; lit?: number; led?: string>`: Port block bolted to a prop's side, 44 x 90 px. (x, y) = its top-left; `lit` 0-1 turns the LED on (glows `led`, default green) once above 0.1.

## `props/crowd.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/props/crowd'`)

> A stadium of tiny sleepers, drawn cheaply: ~1100 people in 25 tiers (one SVG per tier, instanced <use>) so a full-frame crowd renders fast, with a few "hero" real <Critter>s seated in the rows who can lift, speak up and wake. Pan the stand sideways with `pan`; back tiers drift less. Crowd         the stand: tiers, seat boards, floating z tags, and every hero that is still asleep or seated AwakeHer

- `type HeroSpot = {k: number; x: number};`: A hero's seat: front-tier index k (0 = front row, up to about 8 stay big enough to read) and its screen x at `heroPan`.
- `type PlacedHero = {k: number; slot: number; x: number};`: A hero placed on a seat: `slot` is the seat in its tier, `x` the feet position when pan is 0 (add tierShift via heroScreenX for any pan).
- `const CROWD_HEROES: HeroSpot[] = [`: Ten hero seats in front tiers 2-6, clustered mid-screen (the default for Crowd and AwakeHeroes); x is the screen x when heroPan is 130.
- `const placeHeroes = (spots: HeroSpot[] = CROWD_HEROES, heroPan = 130): PlacedHero[] => spots.map((h) => {`: Snap hero spots onto real seats so no sleeper overlaps a hero: pass the same `spots` and `heroPan` you give Crowd and AwakeHeroes.
- `const heroScreenX = (h: PlacedHero, pan: number) => h.x + tierShift(tierOf(h.k), pan);`: Screen x of a placed hero's feet at a given pan; the feet y is that tier's baseline (about 1320 at k 2, 1128 at k 6).
- `type HeroState = {lift?: number; expr?: Expr; armUp?: number; awake?: boolean; wave?: number};`: What a hero is doing this frame: lift (px up off the seat), expression, arms up 0-1, wave (deg), awake (true = AwakeHeroes draws it, Crowd skips it).
- `<Crowd pan?: number; seat?: string; hero?: (i: number) => HeroState; zz?: boolean; heroes?: HeroSpot[]; heroPan?: number; haze?: string; dusk?: string; heroAcc?: Acc>`: The sleeping stadium, full frame. pan = px to scroll (-270..270); hero(i) = state of hero i (index into `heroes`); zz = floating z tags; seat = seat-board colour; haze/dusk = depth fog and mood tint.
- `<AwakeHeroes hero: (i: number) => HeroState; pan?: number; seat?: string; heroes?: HeroSpot[]; heroPan?: number; haze?: string; dusk?: string; heroAcc?: Acc>`: The awake heroes (hero(i).awake), drawn above everything with a brightness lift; use the same pan, seat, heroes, heroPan, haze, dusk and heroAcc as Crowd.

## Backdrops (24 generated sets, `<Backdrop name="..." />` from `'../lib/paper/backdrops'`)

Full-frame 1080x1920 paper-diorama rooms and outdoor sets: use one in place of `<Room>`. Each follows the layout contract: floor line near y 1420,
calm middle band for props, calm top for the banner, plain bottom for captions. Stand props and critters on that backdrop's `floorY`.
Optional `tint` (multiply colour) and `dim` (0-1 darkening) shift a set's mood. No people or text are baked in.

| name | floorY | mood | desc | bestFor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
